required.label: Required
required.detail: A code is asked at login to this client (realm mode {{mode}}; unset counts as required); acr=2.

not_required.detail: Per-client mode, and this client is set to not require TOTP: password only, acr=1. A super admin can change it on the client's page.

off.label: Off (realm)

not_configured.label: Not configured
not_configured.detail: The realm's browser flow is "{{flow}}", not browser-totp — nothing asks for a code yet.

bypassed.label: Bypassed
bypassed.detail: This client overrides the browser flow, so Keycloak runs that flow instead of browser-totp and its users are never asked for a code.

no_user_login.label: n/a

mfa.nowOtherMode: 2FA now {{state}} on {{clientId}} (realm mode is {{mode}}, so this takes effect only in per-client mode).

new.title: New client
new.description: Creates a confidential OAuth2/OIDC client (or SAML when enabled) with PKCE-required and implicit-flow-disabled defaults.
new.clientIdHelp: Used as both the Keycloak clientId and the display name. Must be unique within the realm.
new.redirectHelp: One per line (or comma-separated). Exact-match enforced — trailing slash matters.
new.postLogoutHelp: Keycloak format: ##-separated list. + means "same as redirect URIs".
new.noInstitutions: No active institutions are registered, so this client cannot be scoped to one. It will be created platform-internal — no delegated admin will see it. Onboard an institution and set the scope afterwards.

errors.redirectRequired: At least one redirect URI is required.

scopeForm.title: Who this client is for
scopeForm.explain: An institution's own app is visible and assignable only inside that institution. A cross-cutting app is the platform's, shared with the institutions you name here.
scopeForm.modeInstitutionHint: The owning institution's delegated admins manage it and assign it to their staff.
scopeForm.modeCrossCuttingHint: A platform-wide app. Only a platform admin can change which institutions may use it.
scopeForm.modePlatformHint: For the SSO's own clients. No delegated admin can see or assign it.
scopeForm.ownerHint: The client-id conventionally starts with this slug:
scopeForm.allHint: Includes institutions onboarded later, automatically. Stored as a policy, not as today's list.
scopeForm.selectedHint: Exactly the institutions you tick. A new institution is not included until someone adds it here.

scopeEditor.description: Scope decides who may be given this client; the access assignment decides who currently has it. Only a platform admin can change scope.
scopeEditor.institutionsFailed: The institution list could not be read ({{error}}).
scopeEditor.inferred: This client's owner is being read from its {{prefix}} client-id prefix — it predates institution scoping. Saving records the ownership explicitly.

scopeEditor.confirmTitle: Remove institutions that still use this client?
scopeEditor.confirmExplain: Confirming applies the new scope and withdraws these institutions' access to the client.

access.title: Access — who can log in
access.description: Only the users and groups assigned here may obtain tokens for {{clientId}}. With default-deny on, a client with no assignment blocks all logins (unless it is an exempt control-plane client). Assigning a group grants access to every member of that group.
access.defaultDenyWarning: No users or groups are assigned. Under default-deny, every login to this client is currently rejected. Add at least one user or group below.
access.deniedExplain: People on the deny-list (sso-access-denied-users) are refused whatever else admits them. Restore grants them again and lifts the denial.
access.deniedNotReported: This wrapper does not list denials here; see each user's App access on their page.
access.searchUsers: Search users by username, name, or email…
access.noneInInstitution: No candidates in that institution — clear the institution filter or refine the search.
access.pickerHint: Access is per user — the institution filter only narrows who you see. A user from any institution can be granted this client.
access.denyConfirm: Put {{user}} on the deny-list for {{clientId}}? The denial beats every grant, including through a group, until it is restored.

joinEditor.title: Join key — how the app finds its own users
joinEditor.description: The application already has its own user table, and sub — a Keycloak UUID — appears nowhere in it. So its tokens carry the chosen identifier in the {{claim}} claim and the application looks it up in its own key column. The claim name never changes.
joinEditor.unsetExplain: No column has been chosen, so this client falls back to email — and is not gated on it: a user with no email is let through with a claim the application cannot resolve. Choosing a column turns that into a refusal at the door.
joinEditor.malformed: This client's join-column attribute holds {{value}}, which is not one of the three — someone edited it by hand. Email is in force until a real choice is saved.
joinEditor.sessionsUnknown: Active sessions could not be counted
joinEditor.sessionsExplain: Tokens those sessions already hold keep carrying the previous identifier until they expire — the switch has to be acknowledged.
joinEditor.blocks: Assigned users this key blocks — {{blocked}} of {{checked}}
joinEditor.truncated: Only the first {{checked}} assigned users were checked, so a clean list is not proof of a clean realm.
joinEditor.allUsable: Every assigned user has a usable key.
joinEditor.checkedAgainst: Checked against the key currently in force.
joinEditor.savedBlocked: Join key set to {{column}} (mapper {{mapper}}) — {{count}} assigned user(s) have no usable value.
joinEditor.confirmExplain: Live sessions keep the old key until they expire, and people already matched into the application by the old column are re-keyed at once.

joinKeys.title: Join keys
joinKeys.description: Which identifier each application uses to find its own user records — carried in the join_key claim. A client with nothing recorded is not usable in provisioning and its tokens carry no such claim, so each one needs an explicit choice.
joinKeys.needDecisionHint: Institution and cross-cutting apps. Drive this to zero.
joinKeys.crossCuttingHint: Shared apps: nobody but a platform admin can set these.
joinKeys.invalidHint: Attribute edited by hand to something that is not a column.
joinKeys.nothingChanged: Nothing has changed yet. The row below is waiting on you.
joinKeys.choicesFailed: The available join columns could not be read
joinKeys.choicesFailedHint: {{error}}. The list is readable; nothing can be set until this resolves, because the columns on offer come from the wrapper.
joinKeys.showingAll_one: Showing every client, including {{count}} platform client that belongs to no institution — the SSO's own.
joinKeys.showingAll_other: Showing every client, including {{count}} platform clients that belong to no institution — the SSO's own.
joinKeys.showingScoped_one: Showing the {{count}} client that belongs to an institution or is shared. {{hidden}} platform client(s) hidden.
joinKeys.showingScoped_other: Showing the {{count}} clients that belong to an institution or are shared. {{hidden}} platform client(s) hidden.
joinKeys.empty: No clients are scoped to an institution yet. Give one an owner on its own screen, or onboard an institution — a client nobody owns is invisible to every delegated admin.
joinKeys.footer1: Saving records the column on the client and writes the protocol mapper that produces the claim — the same as for a newly created client. Every change is recorded with who made it and when.
joinKeys.footer2: Changing a column on an app that already has users needs a confirmation: they are matched into the application's records by the old identifier. Open a client's own screen to see which assigned users have no usable value before choosing.

detail.redirectUrisHelp: One per line. Exact-match against /oauth2/authorize requests.
detail.postLogoutDescription: Where Keycloak may send the browser after an RP-initiated logout (post_logout_redirect_uri on /oauth2/logout). Exact-match, like redirect URIs.
detail.postLogoutHelp: One per line. A single + reuses the redirect URIs above. Leave empty to clear (Keycloak then falls back to the redirect URIs).
detail.dangerExplain: Deleting a client invalidates all in-flight tokens for it and breaks any integrator who hasn't migrated to another client_id.

secret.title: Client secret
secret.publicClient: This is a public client (no secret). Public clients authenticate with PKCE alone — there's nothing to reveal or rotate.
secret.description: Reveal the current secret or rotate it. Rotation invalidates the old value immediately — any integrator using it must update their CLIENT_SECRET.
secret.hidden: The secret is hidden. Reveal it to load it, or rotate to generate a new one.
secret.rotateConfirm: Rotate the secret of {{clientId}}? The current secret stops working immediately.

mfa.title: Two-factor authentication (TOTP)
mfa.description: Read by the browser-totp flow at every login. Per client lets each client decide (a client nobody set requires it). Users holding mfa-exempt are never asked. Tokens carry acr=2 when a code was presented, acr=1 otherwise.

off.label: Off
off.hint: No client asks for a code

all.label: All clients
all.hint: Every client asks for a code

mfa.flowNotReady: not browser-totp — the mode has no effect
mfa.superAdminOnly: Only a super admin can change the mode or exemptions.
mfa.bulkStarted: Enrolment was assigned to existing users.

consequences.allEveryone: From their next login, every user who does not hold mfa-exempt must enter a TOTP code, on every application in the realm — whatever an individual client is set to.
consequences.allNoGrace: Users with no authenticator are made to set one up before their login completes. There is no grace period.
consequences.allBulkFirst: This is the first time, so CONFIGURE_TOTP is also assigned to every existing enabled user who has no TOTP credential (never to exempt users).
consequences.allBulkDone: Existing users were already given CONFIGURE_TOTP ({{when}}); it is not assigned again.
consequences.perClientDefault: A client asks for a TOTP code unless a super admin has set it to not required. A client nobody has set requires it.
consequences.perClientStepUp: Someone signed in to an app that does not require a code is asked for one when they open an app that does. Institution admins may turn it on for their own apps, never off.
consequences.perClientNoBulk: No one is bulk-enrolled: each person enrols at their first login to an app that requires it.
consequences.offPasswordOnly: Logins on every client proceed with the password only. Tokens carry acr=1, so applications that check for MFA will see that it did not happen.
consequences.offKept: Existing TOTP credentials and each client's own setting are kept.
consequences.flowNotReady: The realm is not on the browser-totp flow, so this change will be refused. Apply the Terraform (enable_mfa_totp) first.

exemptions.revokeBody: Their next login asks for a TOTP code again.

exemptions.reasonTooLong: The justification is limited to {{max}} characters.

exemptions.reasonHelp: {{min}}–{{max}} characters: who asked, why TOTP cannot be used, until when. Recorded on the user.

smtp.testHelp: The test uses the saved settings — save first.

themes.title: Available themes
themes.description: Themes installed on the Keycloak server. The login theme is the Keycloakify build.

readOnly.description: Managed as code (infra/terraform, configs/realms) — shown here, not edited.

attention.leavers: leavers still have an enabled account or an application
attention.setupEmail: new accounts were never sent their set-password email
attention.locked: people are locked out after failed logins
attention.unlinked: employees have no SSO account yet — granting them an application creates one

matrix.title: Access matrix
matrix.description: Which of {{institution}}'s employees can sign in to which application — including the ones with no SSO account yet, who get one when you grant them an application. Tick cells to build a set of changes, then apply them together.
matrix.exportFailed: The export could not be downloaded
matrix.noApps: This institution has no applications in its scope yet.
matrix.pickHint: Pick up to {{max}}. Each becomes a column of the matrix.
matrix.grantHeadline: Grant mode — tick people who should get access
matrix.revokeHeadline: Revoke mode — tick people whose access you are removing
matrix.readOnlyNote: Your role may view who has access but not change it (it lacks manage-clients). Every cell is read-only.
matrix.search: Search by name, employee number or NID…
matrix.selectColumn: Select every changeable cell for {{client}} on this page
matrix.revealNid: Show the full NID (recorded in the audit log)
matrix.revealedAudited: Every NID you reveal is recorded in the audit log.
matrix.noAccountHint: No SSO account yet. Granting an application creates one.
matrix.leftHint: IPPIS reports no open post here
matrix.resendHint: Email a new set-password link. Any earlier link stops working. Recorded in the audit log.
matrix.resendRefused: {{name}}: the last email did go out — they can ask for a new one from the sign-in page.
matrix.pendingDialogBody: Apply or discard them before switching to {{mode}} mode.
matrix.revokeConfirmBody: These people lose access to these applications. Accounts and institution membership are not touched.
matrix.whyStateChanged: some cells were changed by someone else since this page loaded. Reload to see the current state.
matrix.createdEmailed: {{count}} SSO account(s) created; each was emailed a link to set a password.
matrix.createdNotSentAll: {{count}} SSO account(s) created, but the set-password email could not be sent to them. Use "Resend email" on those rows.
matrix.createdNotSentSome: {{count}} SSO account(s) created, but the set-password email to {{notSent}} could not be sent. Use "Resend email" on those rows.

cell.noManage: Your role in this institution may view access but not change it (manage-clients).
cell.readOnlyColumn: Access to this application is read-only for you.
cell.leaver: IPPIS reports no open post for them here — a leaver is not given access.
cell.alreadyHas: Already has access — switch to Revoke to remove it.
cell.hasNone: Has no access — switch to Grant to give it.
cell.disabledHeader: Nothing here can change in this mode.

setupEmail.failedHint: The set-password email could not be sent. They do not know the account exists.
setupEmail.not_configuredHint: No mail relay was configured when the account was created, so nobody was told.
setupEmail.sentHint: A set-password email was sent. If it was lost, they can get a new one from "Didn't get the email to set your password?" on the sign-in page.
setupEmail.pendingHint: The account is waiting for its first password.

import.title: Import access from a spreadsheet
import.description: Grant applications to {{institution}}'s employees from an exported access matrix that someone has marked up. Imports only grant: a cleared cell is reported, never revoked.
import.step1: Export the matrix from the access matrix and send it to whoever decides.
import.step2: They type YES against each person who should get an application.
import.step3: Upload the file here. You will see exactly what would be granted before anything changes.
import.approvedByPlaceholder: Name and title of the person who signed off this list
import.approvedByHint: Recorded in the audit trail on every grant this import makes.
import.approvedByShort: Name who approved this list (at least 2 characters).
import.confirmGrants: Confirming grants {{count}} application access(es){{created}}. Nothing is revoked.
import.nothingToConfirm: This file grants nothing new — there is nothing to confirm.
import.confirmBefore: Confirm before {{when}}, or upload the file again.
import.doneSummary: {{applied}} granted{{rejected}}{{failed}}. Recorded in the audit log under import {{id}}.

revoke.title: Remove application access
revoke.description: Withdraw access to applications from staff in {{institution}}. This removes the application assignment only — accounts, institution membership and roles are untouched.
revoke.pickUsersHint: Tick the people whose access you are removing. The next step shows what they currently hold.
revoke.holdPairs: They hold {{count}} application assignment(s) between them.
revoke.nothingHeld: None of the selected users currently hold any application in this institution's scope. There is nothing to remove.
revoke.pickAppsHint: Tick the applications to remove. You will see a summary from the server before anything changes.
revoke.allBody: Strips the selected users' access to all {{count}} application assignment(s) they hold across {{institution}}. Destructive and wide-reaching — it needs a typed confirmation.
revoke.allWarning: Every application above will be withdrawn from every user listed. Their accounts remain; a colleague will have to grant each application back individually.
revoke.noHolders: Nobody in this institution can use this application.
revoke.notRevocable: Your tier cannot change access to this application: you can read the list, not act on it.
revoke.groupNote: Access held through a group is withdrawn per person (they are put on the application's deny-list); the group itself is not changed.

summary.nothing: Nothing would change. None of the selected users hold the selected applications — either their access was already removed, or they never had it.
summary.noChangeFor: No change for {{names}} — they do not hold the selected application(s), or their access was already removed.
summary.footer: Removing access withdraws the application assignment only. The accounts, their place in the institution, their roles and every other application are untouched.

list.title: Clients
list.description: Clients belonging to {{institution}} ({{allow}}), plus cross-cutting clients this institution may use. Granting access lets this institution's users sign in to the app.
list.secretNote: Configure it in the application and do not share it further.
list.unconfigured_one: {{count}} of {{total}} clients has no join column set
list.unconfigured_other: {{count}} of {{total}} clients have no join column set
list.unconfiguredBody: Their tokens carry no join_key claim and provisioning refuses them, because nothing has been chosen for them yet. Nothing is defaulted on an application's behalf.
list.readOnly: Read-only: your tier includes view-clients but not manage-clients, so access cannot be changed here.
list.sharedAll: A platform-wide client available to every institution
list.revokeBody: Users in this institution will no longer be able to sign in to that application. Existing sessions continue until they expire.
list.revokeCrossCutting: This is a cross-cutting application: only {{institution}}'s access is removed — other institutions using it are unaffected.
list.empty: No applications are available to this institution yet.
list.emptyManage: Integrate one — it is created as {{institution}}-<app> and belongs to this institution.
list.emptyReadOnly: Your tier can view clients but not integrate one; a platform admin or a colleague with manage-clients can.
list.noteJoinKey: The join key is what an application matches against its own user table. The ones carrying a pencil are yours to change; opening any of them shows which of your staff have no usable value for it.
list.note2fa: 2FA says whether users are asked for a TOTP code when they sign in to the app. The realm setting comes first; when it is per application, you can require it on this institution's own apps, but only a super admin can turn it off again.
list.noteAccess: Access is enforced at token issuance: with default-deny, a client with no assignment rejects every login. Granting here assigns this institution's group to the client. On a cross-cutting client the grant is additive and the revoke removes only this institution.

mfa.unknownHint: The realm's TOTP state could not be read.
mfa.offHint: Two-factor authentication is switched off for the whole realm by a super admin: nobody is asked for a code on any app.
mfa.allHint: The realm requires TOTP on every app: every user who is not mfa-exempt enters a code.
mfa.requiredHint: This app requires TOTP: every user who is not mfa-exempt enters a code at login. Only a super admin can turn this off.
mfa.notRequiredHint: A super admin has turned TOTP off for this app: its users sign in with a password only.
mfa.requireBody: From their next login, users of this application will be asked for a TOTP code; anyone who has not set one up is made to do so before the login completes. Only a super admin can turn it off again.

joinKey.malformedHint: The client's attribute holds "{{value}}", which is not a join column. Choose a real column to replace it.
joinKey.notSetHint: Nothing is recorded on this client: its tokens carry no join_key claim and provisioning refuses it until a column is chosen.
joinKey.explain: Tokens issued to this app carry the chosen identifier in the {{claim}} claim, read from the user's {{source}}. The application looks that value up in its own user table — the claim name never changes, so re-keying an app changes nothing in its code.
joinKey.noneChosen: Nobody has chosen a join key for this app yet, so it falls back to email. Until one is chosen, a user with no email address is not stopped at the door — they arrive at the application with a claim it cannot resolve.
joinKey.malformed: The client carries "{{value}}" as its join column, which is not one of the three. Email is in force; save a real choice to clear it.
joinKey.sessionsUnknown: Active sessions could not be counted
joinKey.sessionsExplain: Changing the key does not change the tokens those sessions already hold — they keep the previous identifier until they expire. If sessions are live or users are already assigned, you will be asked to confirm.
joinKey.crossCuttingReadOnly: This is a cross-cutting app — several institutions use it, so its join key is a platform admin's to set.
joinKey.tierReadOnly: Read-only: your tier does not include manage-clients for this app.
joinKey.blockedAfter_one: {{count}} assigned user cannot sign in until their record is fixed
joinKey.blockedAfter_other: {{count}} assigned users cannot sign in until their records are fixed
joinKey.blockedTitle: Staff who cannot use this key
joinKey.blockedExplain: Everyone assigned to this app, checked against the key in force. A user listed here is refused a token for this app — with a message naming the attribute — rather than handed one the application cannot resolve.
joinKey.truncated: Only the first {{count}} assigned users were checked, so a clean list here is not proof the whole institution is clean.
joinKey.notChecked: The assigned users were not checked.
joinKey.nobodyAssigned: Nobody is assigned to this app yet, so there is nothing to check.
joinKey.allUsable: Every assigned user has a usable key.
joinKey.confirmSessions_one: {{count}} active session keeps the previous key until it expires.
joinKey.confirmSessions_other: {{count}} active sessions keep the previous key until they expire.
joinKey.confirmAssigned_one: {{count}} assigned user is re-matched by the new key.
joinKey.confirmAssigned_other: {{count}} assigned users are re-matched by the new key.

joinKeys.title: Join keys
joinKeys.description: Which identifier each application uses to find its own user records — carried in the join_key claim. A client with nothing recorded is not usable in provisioning, so each one needs an explicit choice.
joinKeys.outstandingHint: Yours to set. Drive this to zero.
joinKeys.platformAdminHint: Cross-cutting apps: shared, so not yours to set.
joinKeys.malformedHint: Attribute edited by hand to something that is not a column.
joinKeys.confirmNote: Nothing has changed yet. The row below is waiting on you.
joinKeys.readOnly: Read-only: your tier includes view-clients but not manage-clients, so you can see what is outstanding but not set it.
joinKeys.crossCuttingHint: A cross-cutting app: several institutions use it, so which identifier it authenticates by is a platform admin's decision.
joinKeys.empty: No applications are in this institution's scope yet.
joinKeys.note1: Saving records the column on the client and writes the protocol mapper that produces the claim. Every change is recorded with who made it and when.
joinKeys.note2: Changing a column on an app that already has users needs a confirmation: they are matched into the application's records by the old identifier, and the switch re-keys all of them at once.

new.title: New client
new.description: Creates a confidential OIDC client owned by {{institution}}. The owning institution is set by the server — you cannot create a client for another institution, or a cross-cutting one, from here.
new.appHelp: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphen. Give the app part only — the client-id becomes {{slug}}-<app>.
new.redirectHelp: One per line (or comma-separated). Exact match — a trailing slash matters.
new.postLogoutHelp: Keycloak's ##-separated list. + means "same as the redirect URIs".
new.nextBody: The client is created with PKCE required and implicit flow disabled. Nobody can sign in to it yet: grant this institution's access on the Clients screen, and collect the client secret there.
new.crossCuttingNote: Need an app several institutions will use? Ask a platform admin to create it as a cross-cutting client including {{institution}}.
new.created: {{clientId}} created — grant access to let your staff sign in.

errors.bad_chars: Use lowercase letters, digits and hyphen only.
errors.has_prefix: Give the app part only — it already starts with "{{slug}}" (e.g. "portal" for {{slug}}-portal).
errors.wildcard_host: "{{uri}}": a wildcard is not allowed in the host.

users.title: Who can use this app
users.description: Users in {{institution}} with access to {{clientId}}{{name}}. Removing access withdraws the application only — it does not delete anyone's account.
users.crossCutting: This is a cross-cutting application: other institutions use it too. Only {{institution}}'s users are listed, and removing access here affects nobody else's staff.
users.readOnly: Read-only: your tier cannot change access on this application.
users.directHint: Assigned to this application by name. Removing access un-assigns them.
users.viaHint: Through the {{group}} group, which the application admits. The group is not changed — this person is recorded as refused on this application instead.
users.empty: Nobody in this institution currently has access to this application.
users.footer_one: {{count}} user with access. Tick the ones to remove — you will see a summary before anything changes.
users.footer_other: {{count}} users with access. Tick the ones to remove — you will see a summary before anything changes.

instAudit.title: Audit log
instAudit.description: Administrative actions recorded for {{institution}} — by this institution's admins and by platform admins acting on its people and apps. Entries are hash-chained and append-only; they cannot be edited or removed. Times are UTC.
instAudit.withheldBody: The audit service returned events outside this institution and the wrapper filtered them out. The audit service is not applying the institution filter — a platform admin should check its deployment.
instAudit.targetPlaceholder: User id, app client id or role
instAudit.noMatch: No audit events match these filters.
instAudit.empty: No audit events yet. Administrative actions on this institution's people and apps will appear here.

list.title: Employees
list.description: {{institution}}'s employees as IPPIS reports them, with or without an SSO account.
list.selectionHint: Your selection is kept while you move between pages and filters.
list.capReached: At most {{max}} employees per run — {{count}} were not added.
list.mirrorOff: The employee list is not available: the wrapper has no employee mirror configured (503).
list.selectPage: Select all selectable employees on this page

block.ambiguous: Matches more than one account — access cannot be changed until IPPIS is corrected.
block.terminated: IPPIS reports no open post — a leaver is not given access.
block.no_email: No account and no email in IPPIS — there is nothing to name an account after.

provision.title: Provision employees
provision.description: Give the selected employees the applications that can identify them, creating accounts for those who have none. Preview first: a dry run writes nothing.
provision.accountsExplain: {{existing}} already have an account (left as it is; applications are added). {{create}} have none and get one named after their email, with a password they set themselves from an emailed link.
provision.unnameable_one: {{count}} selected employee has no account and no email — nothing can be given to them; the report will name them.
provision.unnameable_other: {{count}} selected employees have no account and no email — nothing can be given to them; the report will name them.
provision.appsTitle: Applications they should be able to reach
provision.appsHint: Each application finds its users by one identifier (its join key). An employee without it is refused that application only; one they already reach is skipped.
provision.noApps: No applications you may assign. Integrate one on the Clients screen first.
provision.noJoinKey: no join key chosen — this application can admit nobody until one is set
provision.previewFirst: Run a dry run to see exactly what will happen, then confirm.
provision.previewReady: The preview below is for exactly this selection.

report.summary: {{grants}} application grants, {{held}} already in place, {{denials}} refused. Every refusal names the field that was missing.
report.denyingEveryone: {{clients}} reached nobody in this selection — usually an application with no join key, or a field IPPIS does not send.
report.sharedDev: shared test password — no set-password email
report.mirrorError: not recorded on the employee row

instStaff.title: Users
instStaff.searchPlaceholder: Search by username, email or name…
instStaff.empty: No staff in this institution yet.
instStaff.noMatch: No staff match this search or filter.
instStaff.deactivateBody: Their account is disabled and all active sessions are terminated immediately. The account is kept (not deleted), so this can be reversed by reactivating them.
instStaff.newDescription: Creates an account in {{institution}} and places it in {{group}}. The institution is set by the server — you cannot create staff into another institution from here.
instStaff.idHelpTitle: Why the National ID and phone are here
instStaff.idHelpBody: An application can be configured to find its own user record by National ID, phone or email — its join key, shown on the Clients screen. Whichever it uses has to be on the account and belong to exactly one person: a value another account already holds is refused. The IPPIS reconcile also sources the National ID, so a value left blank here may arrive on its own.
instStaff.noPasswordBody: This console cannot issue or reset credentials — that stays with a platform admin. The account is created active; the staff member cannot sign in until their initial credential is set. Roles are assigned after creation, on the Roles screen.
instStaff.created: {{username}} created — a platform admin must set their initial credential.
instStaff.usernameFixed: The username cannot be changed — it is the account's stable identifier.
instStaff.readOnly: Read-only: your tier does not include manage-members.
instStaff.deactivateExplain: Disables the account and terminates every active session immediately. The account is kept, so this is reversible.
instStaff.rolesDescription: Only your institution's own namespace is assignable: {{allow}}.
instStaff.assignedHint: Roles this staff member holds that you may revoke.
instStaff.availableHint: Every role here is one the API will accept — the list is filtered server-side by the same rule that guards the write.
instStaff.noneAssigned: None of your institution's roles are assigned yet.
instStaff.allGranted: Every role you may assign is already granted.
instStaff.readOnlyRolesHint: Held by this account but not assignable by your tier — only a platform admin can change these.
instStaff.outsideRoles_one: {{count}} role outside your institution's namespace is not shown.
instStaff.outsideRoles_other: {{count}} roles outside your institution's namespace are not shown.
instStaff.rolesPageDescription: The roles you may assign within {{institution}}. Assign or revoke them from a user's Roles screen.
instStaff.denyExplain: Denies are absolute — where you hold several tiers, allows add up but a deny in any of them still wins. A role outside these patterns cannot be granted through this console or its API.
instStaff.noRoles: No assignable roles. A platform admin may need to apply the delegated templates to create this institution's roles.

validation.nid: A National ID is exactly 16 digits.
validation.phone: A phone number is 9–15 digits, optionally with a leading +.
